deities: Goddess Mahalaxmi (Lakshmi, goddess of wealth and prosperity)
Sundar Vinayak (Ganesha) and Rishabhdev - idols installed with Mahalaxmi per local tradition
festivals: Deepotsav - 4-day Diwali celebration from Dhanteras onward (temple's busiest period)
Mahalakshmi Prakat Utsav on Ashtami of Shraddha Paksha

history.period: ~400 years old; built during Maharana Jagat Singh's reign per Shrimali Samaj tradition (17th century) - other accounts credit Maharana Shambhu Singh (19th century) (conflict - verify)
history.summary: One of the few Mahalaxmi temples in Rajasthan, located at Bhatiyani Chohatta in Udaipur's old city near Jagdish Temple. Tradition holds it was built about 400 years ago during Maharana Jagat Singh's reign using leftover stone and materials from the construction of the Jagdish Temple (the Ganesh temple in front was likewise built from this temple's leftover materials); other accounts credit 19th-century Maharana Shambhu Singh instead (builder and period conflict - verify). The idol of Mahalaxmi, seated on a white-stone elephant, is said to have been brought from Bhinmal (ancient Shrimal); she is the kuldevi (family deity) of the Shrimali community, whose trust manages the temple. Devotees throng the temple during Deepotsav, when Diwali crowds queue for darshan and the Bhatiyani Chohatta area is illuminated.

name: Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Udaipur, the former capital of the Mewar kingdom, is one of Rajasthan's major tourist cities - the 'City of Lakes' built around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, with the City Palace, Jagdish Temple (about 0.5 km from this temple) and old-city bazaars. It is a major rail junction with its own airport, about 390 km from Jaipur.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 20-25 km from the temple (verify).
travel.railway: Udaipur City Railway Station, about 2-3 km away (verify).
travel.road: At Bhatiyani Chohatta near Rao Ji Ka Hata Road in the old city, about 0.5 km from Jagdish Temple; walkable from the City Palace area, or a short auto ride.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Diwali (Deepotsav) if you want the festival atmosphere - expect very heavy crowds then.
